title: Shrink the 6 functions in go/internal/setup and go/internal/releasepipeline over the 50-line limit and drop them from the size ratchet's offender list
summary: The repo-wide size ratchet (go/internal/sizeratchet, cycle 1726) lists every function over 50 lines with an allowance that may only shrink. These are the listed offenders in go/internal/setup and go/internal/releasepipeline: internal/releasepipeline.defaultReleaseVerify (60 lines), internal/releasepipeline.newReleaseRun (62 lines), internal/releasepipeline.releaseRun.prePublish (68 lines), internal/setup.Apply (63 lines), internal/setup.Detect (104 lines), internal/setup.Recommend (65 lines). Each should do one thing at one level of abstraction (Clean Code, skills/engineering-craft/references/clean-code.md): extract named steps until every function is 50 lines or fewer, with behavior unchanged. Since 2026-09-28 (fix/sizeratchet-is-a-ceiling) an allowance is a ceiling: this lane shrinks the functions to 50 lines or fewer and leaves their offenders.json entries as slack for the boundary tighten; it does not edit offenders.json (two shrink lanes' keys sit on adjacent lines and would conflict at the fleet rebase).
acceptance: Behavior is unchanged: the package's existing tests pass unmodified; a function without a test that pins its behavior gets a characterization test first, red on a mutant.
No comments are added (docs/conventions/code-comments.md); names carry the intent.
The shrunk functions measure 50 lines or fewer (sizeratchet.Walk); offenders.json is left unchanged and the module-wide ratchet stays green
priority_rationale: wave 21 boundary 2026-09-28: real clean-code debt the ratchet now tracks; lane-sized, behavior-preserving refactors on non-protected packages
